ov: A wild pig of the grasslands and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, with two pairs of upward-curving tusks. The short lower pair is kept razor-sharp by rubbing against the upper pair.

why.dg: Warthogs use their razor-sharp lower tusks in fights and to defend themselves against predators.
why.et: Valued for its meat, both locally and in city markets, and popular on game ranches.

df: Grasses, bulbs and roots, dug up with its snout and feet.

cf.tip: Both are wild pigs; the warthog is African, with two pairs of upward-curving tusks.

fx: When feeding it often kneels on its front wrists, which have calloused pads from before birth.
notes: The existing fact (reverses into its burrow) is confirmed.
